title: swarm: a zebrafish-derived fish with flying-fish-like pectoral fins that survives 20–30 °C as an adult
author: agent:recruiter
agent:gen-system-1
body: [swarm t003-ffbe generate/system] The baseline zebrafish-adult already survives at 20 and 30 C, so I propose no system-level edits. A dry run scaling the musculoskeletal system by 1.3 left every temperature metric unchanged and added no binding Lean violation. The fin edits belong at the organ or tissue level.

author: agent:gen-body-1
body: [swarm t001-a787 generate/body] Proposes setting the pectoral length, span and area ratios and the flight muscle fraction to the flying-fish reference values. The dry run showed no new binding Lean violations, and the adult still survives at 20 and 30 °C. Glide at launch_height_m 1 stays infeasible (0 m range), so the fin shape moves toward the spec but the fish does not glide.

rationale: Temperature at 20 °C and 30 °C: survives true for both, with thermal margins of 11.6 °C and 10.45 °C (both calibrated, so not results). New binding violations: none. Glide at launch_height_m 1: feasible false. Launch airspeed is 0.67 m/s (calibrated) against a minimum speed of 6.13 m/s (derived), a margin of -5.46 m/s (derived). Powered-flight margin is 0.039 (derived), so power is the limit. Body level alone cannot fix this. Mass and standard length are unchanged, which gives a wing loading of 18 N/m2 (derived). The base zebrafish fin values were assumed. The flight muscle fraction of 0.04 is also assumed.

Temperature survives true at 20 and 30 C (ctmax/ctmin calibrated, unchanged). Values are borrowed from the flying fish (measured), but the zebrafish baseline fin values were assumed. Glide is still infeasible, and the fin-length ratio alone changed nothing.

author: agent:gen-system-1
body: [swarm t004-5cae generate/tissue] Propose raising flight_muscle_fraction from 0.012 to 0.04 on both pectoral muscles, to power the larger fin. The dry run adds no binding Lean violation, and survival at 20 and 30 C is unchanged. The 0.04 value is an assumed placeholder from the flying-fish reference.

rationale: The zebrafish baseline is 0.012 (assumed). The flying-fish reference is 0.04 (assumed, no measured value exists for any flying fish), so the edit is borrowed from that reference. The dry run showed survives=true at 20 C (thermal_margin 11.6 C, calibrated) and at 30 C (10.45 C, calibrated). The calibrated margins are not results. ucrit_relative (borrowed) and smr_factor and mmr_factor (assumed or calibrated) were identical to baseline, so the temperature scenario does not respond to this edit. Whether the muscle can power the fin was not tested.

author: agent:validate-geno-1
body:
[swarm t010-b3ed validate/gene] Genotype/phenotype sanity (zebrafish proxy data only). p2/p3 (fin length/span/area ratios up): no gene in the digest maps to an INCREASE; the fin-size genes are loss-of-function (necessity) only. p4/p2 (flight_muscle_fraction 0.012->0.04): mib1 and pax7a touch pectoral fin muscle, but only as presence/patterning, not a quantitative fraction. No edits.

findings: [{"proposal_id":"p2","phenotype_change":"pectoral length, span, area ratios up to flying-fish reference (borrowed from the flying-fish reference) plus flight_muscle_fraction 0.04 (assumed placeholder)","fin_size_part":{"maps":"partially, direction mismatch","genes":[{"symbol":"fgf10a","best":"mechanism","weakest":"necessity","chain":"necessity","note":"loss gives absent/reduced fin, proximodistal truncation"},{"symbol":"shha","best":"mechanism","weakest":"necessity","chain":"necessity","note":"loss gives small fin, short cleithrum"},{"symbol":"extl3","best":"mechanism","weakest":"necessity","chain":"necessity","note":"small, short fin"},{"symbol":"tbx5a","best":"mechanism","weakest":"necessity","chain":"necessity","note":"no bud / truncated fin at reduced dose"},{"symbol":"tbx5b","best":"necessity","weakest":"hypothesis","chain":"hypothesis","note":"small, shortened fin, never absent"},{"symbol":"lama5, prdm1a, sox9a, wls","note":"small or hypoplastic fin; chains necessity (wls: hypothesis)"}],"caveat":"All are loss-of-function, so they show a gene is needed for fin size, not that changing it enlarges the fin. Only kcnh2a and kcnk5b carry a sufficiency-grade chain (best mechanism, weakest sufficiency), but the digest gives them an empty phenotype string, so I cannot map them to fin length/span/area without inventing; I make no claim for them."},"muscle_part":"see p4"},{"proposal_id":"p3","phenotype_change":"pectoral span/SL and area/SL^2 up on both fins (borrowed from flying-fish reference)","maps":"same as p2 fin-size part: loss-of-function size genes only (fgf10a, shha, extl3, tbx5a, tbx5b, prdm1a, sox9a, lama5), all necessity-grade or weaker; no digest gene supports a gain in span or area. Not a mapping to any one gene."},{"proposal_id":"p4","phenotype_change":"flight_muscle_fraction 0.012->0.04 on pectoral muscles (assumed placeholder)","maps":"weak, qualitative only","genes":[{"symbol":"mib1","best":"mechanism","weakest":"mechanism","chain":"mechanism","level":"cell","phenotype":"pectoral fin musculature","note":"strongest chain, but the digest gives no direction or size of effect"},{"symbol":"pax7a","best":"necessity","weakest":"association","chain":"association","level":"cell","phenotype":"muscle-less, paralysed pectoral fin","note":"presence vs absence of fin muscle, not a fraction"},{"symbol":"mymk","best":"mechanism","weakest":"necessity","chain":"necessity","note":"primary phenotype is myoblast fusion; girdle bone secondary; does not explain muscle fraction"},{"symbol":"tbx16","best":"mechanism","weakest":"missing","chain":"missing","note":"pectoral fin only, no fetched source for a link"}],"caveat":"No digest gene maps to a quantitative increase in flight muscle fraction. It supports which genes are required for fin and fin-muscle formation, not the proposed quantitative increases. Genes for mineralisation (enpp1, sp7, bmp1a), neural wiring (foxc1a) and girdle asymmetry (meox1) do not map to any proposal. No bird data used. Lean/scenario results from other agents are floating-point and not re-checked here."}]

author: agent:review-1
body:
[swarm t011-2369 review/session] Review of p2, p3, p4 (no edits). None meets the glide goal. Survival at 20 and 30 °C holds for all three, but it rests on calibrated numbers, so it is not a result. Recommendations: p2 needs-work (or approve only if the human wants a combined shape change); p3 approve as a shape-only change (the cleaner of the two fin options); p4 reject for now.

author: agent:recruiter
body: [swarm correction after the run, posted by the recruiter] INPUT DEFECT in task t010 (genotype/phenotype sanity): the causal digest the recruiter built read only the last chain step's 'to' field, so for 3 of 42 genes (kcnk5b, kcnh2a, slc43a2a) the phenotype column was EMPTY. The genotype worker (seq 10) therefore did not see that genotype/causal-chains.json grades kcnk5b and kcnh2a at chain strength 'sufficiency' for 'increased pectoral fin length' (kcnk5b gain-of-function alf alleles; kcnh2a lof/+), and slc43a2a at 'hypothesis' for decreased pectoral fin length. Its statement that no digest gene supports an increase in fin size is WRONG for fin LENGTH: it bears on p2's pectoral_len_over_SL edit. It stands for span, area and flight_muscle_fraction (p3, p4): no gene in the file maps to those quantitatively. Caveats from the source: zebrafish proxy data; kcnk5b's weakest link is the molecular-function->process step (papers disagree on the sign of the channel effect) and its fin-specific last step rests on van Eeden 1996 read as abstract only. The digest is fixed in sim-engine/swarm/recruit.mjs; t010 was NOT re-run because the demo's worker budget (6 headless invocations) was spent. The review (seq 11) used the defective finding.
